title: The Alchemist’s Dark Vault

narrative.arrival: The vault door grinds shut behind you. Somewhere ahead a chest clicks open, but you cannot see a thing. A brass claw waits for its number.
narrative.sealed: Three torches blaze. In their light the goblin bows, beaten at its own game, and the way to the courtyard opens.

inscription:
The vault is too dark to see into the chest. Inside are 12 ruby crystals, 12 sapphire crystals and 12 emerald crystals, all mixed up. The claw picks without looking.

Each torch starts with a full chest. The claw picks one crystal at a time. Do not put any crystals back until that torch is finished. Choose the smallest number of grabs that will always meet the torch’s goal, even with the worst luck.

parts.prompt: Torch of Pairs: What is the smallest number of grabs that will always give you at least 2 crystals of the same colour?

misconceptions.probe: Two grabs might match, or they might not. Picture Grubb inside the chest handing you the crystals: what would it hand you to spoil your pair?
You stopped at the number of colours. Can Grubb still keep every grab a different colour at that point, and what happens on the grab after that?
You planned to grab until a whole colour is gone. Is that needed for one matching pair, or could a pair appear far earlier?
What does certain mean here: that a pair is possible, or that a pair cannot be avoided?

l0: My lantern runs on oil, not luck. For this torch, are we hunting for a pair that might appear on a lucky grab, or a pair that cannot be avoided?
Let's read the torch's demand before opening the chest. What must be true for a grab to count as certain, no matter how unlucky we are?
Grubb would like us to rely on luck. Look at the inscription: is it asking what could happen, or what must happen every single time?
l1: Picture Grubb inside the chest, choosing each crystal to delay our torch. What would he hand you on each grab to keep a pair from appearing?
Lemma has a card for a day when luck refuses to help. Which card in the Deck could help us think about the unluckiest case?
Let's try a chest small enough for my workbench, with only two colours. How long could Grubb keep every crystal you grab a different colour?

l2.text: A bin for each colour gives us a place to keep watch. Grubb uses empty bins to avoid a pair. Once every bin holds one crystal, what must the next crystal do?

l4.statement: A tiny chest has 5 red and 5 blue crystals. How many grabs make a matching pair certain?
l4.l3: The goblin gives you one red, then one blue. Whatever comes next matches one of them. Count the grabs.

l3.text: Put one crystal in each bin on the blueprint, leaving Grubb no empty bin to choose. What happens when the next crystal has to join an occupied bin?

understand: The claw must sometimes get a pair
The claw must always get a pair, however unlucky
We need to empty one colour
I am not sure what certain means here
plan: Pretend a goblin picks for me

parts.prompt: Torch of Four: What is the smallest number of grabs that will always give you at least 4 crystals of the same colour?

intermediates.label: most crystals without club of four

misconceptions.probe: Four was the number for a pair. This torch wants a bigger club of one colour. How many of each colour could Grubb hand over while still dodging that club?
You found how many Grubb can hand out while every colour stays below the club size. What must the very next grab do?
Do you need a whole colour gone, or only enough that Grubb runs out of ways to dodge?
Say in your own words what Grubb is trying to avoid this time?

l0: New torch, new demand. Let's put it in our own words: does it want four crystals of every colour, or four crystals of any single colour?
My notebook has room for the torch's demand. How many crystals of a single colour must the claw secure, however Grubb chooses them?
Grubb has taken his place beside the chest again. Looking at this torch's demand, what is he trying to prevent as he hands over crystals?
l1: Lemma has kept the unluckiest-case card handy. Can we use it to fill each colour short of the goal before any colour reaches the club size?
Let Grubb make the choices on our blueprint. How many crystals could he give you of each colour without completing a club of four?
A goblin needs somewhere to hide the next crystal. What happens if he has handed out as many as possible without any colour reaching the target?

l2.text: Grubb fills each bin one below the club size so no bin reaches the goal. Once every bin is filled that way, where can the next crystal go?

l4.statement: A tiny chest has 5 red and 5 blue crystals. How many grabs make three of one colour certain?
l4.l3: The goblin gives two of each colour. The next grab must complete three of a colour. Count them.

l3.text: On the blueprint, fill each bin until it is one crystal short of four. Then let Grubb choose a bin for a final grab. What does that grab force to happen?

understand: The claw needs four of every colour
The claw needs four crystals of any single colour
We must grab every crystal in the chest
I am not sure what a club of four means
plan: Fill each colour to one below four
Grab crystals at random and hope
Try a tiny chest with fewer colours

parts.prompt: Torch of Difference: What is the smallest number of grabs that will always give you at least 2 crystals of different colours?

misconceptions.probe: Same number as the pair torch, but this torch wants two different colours. What is Grubb's best trick now to keep every crystal the same?
Two grabs might differ, or they might match. Picture Grubb inside the chest: what would it hand you?
You counted a whole colour. If Grubb hands you every crystal of one colour, what colour is the grab after that?
What is the opposite of what Grubb tried in the earlier torches?

l0: The Torch of Difference has its own demand. Before we open the chest, how many different colours must we be certain to hold in our hand?
Let's give this torch a fresh line in the notebook. In your own words, what does the Torch of Difference ask us to guarantee?
Grubb is choosing again, so luck gets no say. What would the unluckiest hand look like when we want crystals of two different colours?
l1: Grubb wants to keep a second colour out of your hand. If he controls each grab from the chest, which crystals will he keep handing you?
Let's check the limits of Grubb's plan. Could he keep giving you the very same colour until that whole colour runs completely out?
Lemma has opened the unluckiest-case card again. What trick would keep every crystal in your hand the same colour for as long as possible?

l2.text: This time Grubb hands over the same colour for as long as the chest allows. How long can he keep that up, and what must happen on the next grab?

l4.statement: A tiny chest has 5 red and 5 blue crystals. How many grabs make two different colours certain?
l4.l3: Give the goblin all 5 red crystals. The next grab must be blue. Count the grabs.

l3.text: Give Grubb every crystal of one colour on the blueprint, then let him hand them over until none remain. What colour must his next crystal be?

understand: The claw needs all crystals of the same colour
The claw needs at least two different colours in the haul
We need to empty the entire chest
I am not sure how difference works

lookBack.prompt: Suppose the chest also held 12 amber crystals, a fourth colour. How many grabs make a matching pair certain now?
Why did Pairs need so few grabs compared with Difference?

options: Pairs, because the goblin has only three ways to dodge
Difference, because the goblin can hide inside one colour for a long time
Four, because four is bigger than two

lookBack.prompt: Think of the Pairs torch as grabs the goblin can waste. How many can it waste before it must give you a pair?

codex.oneLine: If there are more crystals than bins, some bin holds two.
